node_definition.done_when:
Read section 3 with read_plan(view='section', section='s3') before starting; it is the authority. The stop path (--hook stop) is NOT part of this node; leave it behaving as on main. reckon/hooks/coordinator_obligations.py's prompt path loads reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py by file path, through importlib.util.spec_from_file_location, registering it in sys.modules before exec_module. It must not import the reckon.crew package, whose __init__ eagerly imports every crew module. It reads the session's snapshot and calls freshness() and live_payload(). A fresh snapshot goes through the hook's existing formatting and injection unchanged, including the digest that suppresses an unchanged list. A snapshot that is not fresh emits the one line naming the reason and the remedy, reckon crew watch --ensure --project PROJECT. The hook never writes the snapshot, and it exits 0 in every case. In a new tests/test_obligations_hook_reads_the_snapshot.py cover four cases: the import surface, where a fresh subprocess runs the prompt path against a temporary configuration home and lists sys.modules, asserting that none of reckon._plan_html, reckon._backends or reckon.ledger is present; each not-fresh reason producing its line, with the snapshot file unchanged afterwards; a reused pid read as not fresh; and a fresh snapshot formatted as today's output. Execute the named negative control. Record as measurement, not as an assertion: 20 consecutive prompt-hook invocations, each a fresh process, against a temporary configuration home holding one fresh snapshot. Write all 20 wall times to a log in the run directory and state the second-slowest; the plan's target is under 250 ms. The gate is the new test plus every test file under tests/ that names coordinator_obligations, found by a text search. Run it at base and at head and list the files in the manifest. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/the-obligations-hook-reads-a-snapshot/hook-reads-the-snapshot.html records the change and the 20 timings.
Run `date -u` first and treat that instant as your start; your deadline is 60 minutes later. Write your manifest before starting any long command. Run both gate arms with pytest-xdist (-n 8 --timeout=300), never serially. Run the base arm, from a `git archive` extraction of your base under /tmp in a directory named for this run, and then the head arm, each in the foreground: a background command dies when your turn ends. Keep the gate to the test files that reach your change, tens of files rather than hundreds. Each arm uses its own basetemp outside any repository and writes to its own new log path, which it never overwrites. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder. Each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
